review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–175) and checked it for repeated proof blocks. The candidates were the lawfulness proofs (`id_map`, `comp_map`, `id_traverse`, `traverse_eq_map_id`, `comp_traverse`, `naturality`). Each of these is a one- to three-line `simp` or `rw` that unfolds `Equiv.map` or `Equiv.traverse` and applies the matching law of `t`. They share no substantial argument. `lawfulFunctor'` uses a `cases F; congr` argument that `isLawfulTraversable'` deliberately does not reuse, because `h₂` needs a `LawfulApplicative` assumption. The four `rw [h₂, ...]` lines in `isLawfulTraversable'` are short one-line applications. A helper lemma for them would save little, so they do not meet the rubric's threshold. I did not search other files for further repeats, because nothing in the target is large enough to anchor a finding.
